tripod.name: The Golden Tripod
tripod.says: Hephaestus's tripod from the Iliad, in polished gold on its golden wheels, a quiet flame in its bowl: the first maker's helpers that move by themselves.

disc.name: The Phaistos Disc
disc.says: The fired clay disc of Phaistos, its spiral of signs pressed into the clay as the potter stamped them, standing in a slender gold stand; it turns very slowly, as a reader follows the spiral.

column.name: The Minoan Column
column.says: A column of the Cretan palaces, widening as it rises: polished gold under a glossy black cushion and an ivory abacus, crowned with the gold horns of consecration, on stepped ivory marble.

phi.name: The Carved Phi
phi.says: The first letter of Phaistos cut in polished gold as a sculptor would cut it: each stroke with two facets meeting at a sharp ridge, its stem standing proud of its bowl, a solid letter whose depth shows as it turns.
